rules.title: Custom-DST ref with [T] slice tail is a 16-byte {data,len} fat pointer
rules.statement: A reference to a custom-DST struct whose last field is a literal slice tail `[T]` (or unsized slice) is represented as a 16-byte fat pointer {data: ptr, len: i64}, the element count carried inline. The length is part of the reference value, not stored in the pointee.

rules.title: Ref to a struct with a dyn tail is a thin 8-byte pointer
rules.statement: A reference whose pointee struct has a `dyn`-tail (e.g. `&RcInner<dyn>`) is physically thin (single 8-byte pointer); the vtable lives in the heap object rather than in the reference, distinguishing it from the 16-byte {data,len} custom-DST fat reference.

rules.title: Ref to a #[self_describing] DST is a thin 8-byte pointer
rules.statement: A reference to a `#[self_describing]` DST is physically thin (8-byte pointer straight to the header); the tail length is recovered in-band from the pointee header rather than carried alongside the pointer.
rules.divergence: Logos custom-DST extension (#[self_describing]); no Rust equivalent.

rules.title: Trait object is a 16-byte {data, vtable} fat pair
rules.statement: A trait object (`dyn Trait`) has value representation as a 16-byte fat pair {data_ptr, vtable_ptr}. `&dyn`/`&mut dyn` are this value-fat-pair on the stack; an owning trait object (Box<dyn>, *const/*mut dyn) is held via an 8-byte heap handle to such a 16-byte pair.

rules.title: Box<dyn Trait> has the same repr as &dyn, differing only by ownership
rules.statement: `Box<dyn Trait>` is not a Box<TraitObject> struct; it is an owning bare trait object with the identical 16-byte {data, vtable} fat-pair representation as `&dyn Trait`. The two differ only in ownership: dropping an owning trait object calls vtable[0] (drop_in_place) then deallocates `data`.

rules.title: Drop recurses structurally by type shape
rules.statement: Dropping a value recurses by type: a struct runs its user `impl Drop` then drops each field; a tuple drops each element; an enum drops the payload of the active variant; an array drops each element; a reference/pointer/scalar drops nothing. Nesting (array-of-struct, struct-with-array-field) is handled recursively.

rules.title: Owner drop runs user Drop then drops fields; nested by-value self stops at user Drop
rules.statement: At the top level (owner semantics), after a value's user `impl Drop` runs, its fields/payload are ALSO dropped by the owner. A nested (non-top-level) drop calls only the user `impl Drop` and stops, because the by-value `self` consumes its own fields at the drop body's scope end.

rules.title: Moved-out sub-values are skipped during drop
rules.statement: Drop of a value suppresses sub-values that were moved out: a dotted path (relative to the value) whose segment exactly matches a child skips that child's drop entirely; a deeper path recurses into the child with the remainder so only the moved leaf is suppressed while its siblings still drop.

rules.title: Drop of owning Box<dyn> calls vtable[0], frees data, frees handle
rules.statement: Dropping an owning `Box<dyn Trait>` whose binding storage is the 8-byte heap handle to a 16-byte {data, vtable} fat pair runs (null-guarded): load data and vtable; call vtable[0](data) (drop_in_place: concrete destructor + owned fields); free(data); free(handle).

rules.title: Drop of owning Box<[T]> drops each element then frees the buffer
rules.statement: Dropping an owning `Box<[T]>` fat slice (value {data, len}) drops each element via a runtime loop over `len` (only when T is droppable) and then frees the heap buffer.

rules.title: Drop of owning Box<Foo> custom-DST drops prefix + tail then frees
rules.statement: Dropping an owning custom-DST `Box<Foo>` drops the droppable prefix fields plus the tail elements (runtime loop over the fat-pointer length carried in the {data, len} pair) and then frees the block.

rules.title: Move-out drop of an unsized dyn tail runs vtable[0] only
rules.statement: Dropping the concrete payload behind a `&dyn` fat pair in place (the move-out drop of an unsized `dyn` tail) runs only vtable[0](data) (the concrete Drop) with NO free and NO refcount change; the underlying block is freed separately by the owner.

rules.title: Concrete value unsized to a fat dyn handle when the destination slot is a trait object
rules.statement: When a destination slot has trait-object type (`dyn`/`Box<dyn>`/`&dyn`) but the supplied value is still concrete (`Box<Concrete>`, `&Concrete`, struct value), the value is unsize-coerced into a fat {data, vtable} handle (e.g. an enum-variant payload typed `Box<dyn>` constructed from `Box<Concrete>`). It is a no-op if the value already is a trait object.

rules.title: Trait-object vtable slot 0 is drop_in_place; supertrait vtables nested
rules.statement: A trait object's vtable carries the concrete type's drop_in_place at slot 0 (called for dynamic destruction) and includes super-vtable pointer slots for each supertrait, each pointing at the supertrait's vtable global.
rules.uncertainty: Slot-0 = drop is stated by the drop-sequence comments; exact remaining vtable slot ordering is not specified in this unit.
